note: The catalogue behind the trust chain and the what-if answers: the actors that stand between a token holder and the company, the rights flows that run between them, how firm a link can be, and the failure modes we ask every issuer to answer. One shared list, so that every issuer answers the same questions and a gap is visible as a gap. Answers live in each dossier's `whatIf[]` (schema in `whatIfSchema` below) and are never invented: an outcome is `documented` only with the source's own words, `inferred` when the structure implies it and we say so, `litigated` when a court or regulator decided it, `unknown` when we looked and the documents do not say. Read by stocks/lib/trustchain.mjs, stocks/load-db.mjs and the pages.

actors.label: Holder
actors.description: The person or entity holding the token: their keys, their venue account, their jurisdiction, their tax residence and their status under sanctions and eligibility rules.

actors.label: Wallet or venue
actors.description: Where the holder keeps and trades the token: a self-custody wallet, a centralised venue or broker account (Kraken, Bybit, Backpack, Alpaca), or a DEX pool. A venue account means the venue, not the holder, controls the keys.

actors.label: Token program and keys
actors.description: The on-chain instrument: the Token-2022 mint, its extensions (freeze, permanent delegate, transfer hook, allowlist, pausable, scaled UI multiplier) and whoever holds the mint, freeze and delegate authorities. This is where the issuer's powers over a holder's tokens are actually exercised.

actors.label: Token issuer
actors.description: The legal entity whose obligation the token is: an SPV, a trust, an LLC series, a note issuer, or (for registered shares) the company itself. It sets the terms, holds or claims the underlying, and answers for redemption.

actors.label: Tokenization provider
actors.description: The operator that runs the platform on the issuer's behalf: mints and burns, onboards, runs the allowlist, publishes prices. It may be the issuer's parent (Kraken for Backed), a regulated transfer agent (Superstate, Securitize) or a third party under a services agreement.

actors.label: Transfer agent
actors.description: For registered-share tokens, the SEC-registered agent that keeps the shareholder register and can convert between on-chain and book-entry form. Without one, the token is not the share.

actors.label: Security agent or trustee
actors.description: The party that holds a pledge or trust over the underlying for the benefit of holders and enforces it if the issuer fails. When there is none, holders are unsecured creditors.

actors.label: Custodian or prime broker
actors.description: The bank or broker that actually holds the underlying shares (or the cash, for synthetics): Alpaca, Interactive Brokers, a Swiss bank, a DTC participant. Its insolvency and its lending practices decide whether the backing is really there.

actors.label: Attestor or oracle
actors.description: Whoever verifies that the backing exists and publishes it: an accounting firm, a proof-of-reserve feed, an auditor. Also the price oracle a venue relies on.

actors.label: Underlying company
actors.description: The company whose stock the token tracks or is: listed (Apple, Nvidia) or private (SpaceX, OpenAI). Its corporate actions, dividends, votes and fate flow down the chain, or do not.

actors.label: Reference market
actors.description: The primary market or price source the token's price refers to: the listing exchange, a private-market mark, an issuer's own valuation. Determines what the token is worth when it cannot be redeemed.

actors.label: Law, regulator and courts
actors.description: The governing law, the regulator that licenses or exempts the issuer, the forum a dispute goes to, and the sanctions and eligibility regimes that decide who may hold at all.

actors.label: Solana network
actors.description: The ledger itself. An outage, a fork or a program upgrade affects transfers, redemptions with deadlines and on-chain corporate actions.

flows.label: Ownership of the underlying
flows.carries: The share (or the cash that stands in for it) and the holder's claim on it: registered share, tracker certificate, debt note, trust entitlement, synthetic exposure, or nothing.

flows.label: Security interest
flows.carries: A pledge, charge or trust over the underlying for holders' benefit, and who enforces it.

flows.label: Issuance and redemption
flows.carries: Subscription and redemption: who may, on what terms, in what currency, at what price, how fast, and what KYC stands in the way.

flows.label: Transfer and control
flows.carries: Who may hold and send the token, and what the issuer can do to a holder's account: allowlist, freeze, pause, permanent delegate, transfer hook.

flows.label: Dividends and cash entitlements
flows.carries: Cash dividends, reinvestment into more units, rebasing multipliers, withholding tax, and liquidity-event proceeds for private companies.

flows.label: Voting and information rights
flows.carries: Whether the holder can vote, who votes the shares held by the custodian, and whether the holder receives shareholder communications.

flows.label: Corporate actions
flows.carries: Splits, reverse splits, spin-offs, rights issues, mergers, acquisitions, delistings and the company's own insolvency, and how each is mirrored (or not) on-chain.

flows.label: Price and reserve verification
flows.carries: The reference price, the proof that the backing exists, and the venues that quote it.

flows.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure
flows.carries: The licence or exemption the issuer relies on, who is allowed to hold, what must be disclosed, and how terms may change.

linkGrades.note: Two independent axes per link, computed by stocks/lib/trustchain.mjs from the dossier's claims and fields, never typed by hand. Colour is `evidence`, line style is `verification`.

evidence.documented: The link rests on at least one `confirmed` claim: the source's own words were read and quoted.
evidence.inferred: Our reading of the structure (`inference` claims), not the source's words.
evidence.asserted: Written down but nobody has checked since (`unverified`), or the only source is the issuer's marketing.
evidence.unknown: Nothing found for the fields this link rests on.

verification.onchain: Verified on the ledger (authority keys, extension state, multiplier, supply).
verification.attested: A third party attests it (accounting firm, proof-of-reserve feed, regulator filing).
verification.none: Not verifiable from where we stand.

answerStatuses.documented: The issuer's or regulator's own document addresses this case; `quote` holds the words, `url` and `locator` find them again.
answerStatuses.inferred: The documents do not address the case directly but the structure implies the answer (for example: bearer token, no allowlist, therefore stolen keys mean stolen tokens). Labelled as our reading.
answerStatuses.litigated: A court, tribunal or regulator decided this or a materially identical case; `cases[]` cites it. The outcome is what was decided, not what we think should happen.
answerStatuses.unknown: We looked and the documents do not say. `searched[]` records where we looked, so the gap itself is evidence.
answerStatuses.not-applicable: The case cannot arise for this structure (no dividends exist for a perpetual; no transfer agent for a tracker certificate). Say why in `note`.

whatIfSchema.note: One entry per failure mode per dossier, in the dossier's `whatIf[]`. Same evidence discipline as `claims[]`: quote, url, locator, accessedAt. `outcome` is one to three sentences in our words, from the holder's point of view, and must not go beyond what `status` licenses.

fields.outcome: what happens to the holder, one to three sentences; for `unknown`, what we could not establish
fields.quote: verbatim words from the source (documented, litigated); null otherwise
fields.locator: page, section, clause or anchor within the source
fields.accessedAt: ISO timestamp of when the source was read
fields.cases: array of {name, court, date, url, holding} for `litigated`, else []
fields.searched: array of URLs or document titles searched, for `unknown` and `inferred`
fields.note: anything the reader needs: caveats, the inference chain, a conflicting document

failureModes.question: My private keys are stolen and the tokens are moved. Can they be recovered, frozen or reissued?
failureModes.lookFor: Lost-token, replacement or reissuance clauses; whether the freeze authority or permanent delegate is ever used for a holder's benefit; allowlist (a thief's wallet cannot receive an allowlisted token); the transfer agent's lost-certificate procedure for registered shares.

failureModes.question: I still hold my keys but was defrauded: a fake token, a fake redemption site, a social-engineered transfer. Does the issuer or venue offer any recourse?
failureModes.lookFor: Disclaimers about impostor tokens and phishing; the canonical mint list the issuer publishes; liability limits in the terms; whether the issuer will freeze a fraudster's account.

failureModes.question: I die. Can my heirs claim the tokens, transfer them or redeem them? Is a probate process recognised?
failureModes.lookFor: Succession or estate clauses; KYC re-onboarding of heirs; allowlist transfer to a new holder; for registered shares, the transfer agent's estate transfer procedure.

failureModes.question: A court orders my tokens transferred, frozen or seized (divorce, judgment, bankruptcy of the holder). Can the issuer comply, and will it?
failureModes.lookFor: Clauses on compliance with court orders and legal process; freeze and delegate powers; whether the issuer treats the token as property it can move on a third party's instruction.

failureModes.question: I move to a jurisdiction where the token is not offered (for example I become a US person). Can I keep it, sell it, redeem it?
failureModes.lookFor: Eligibility clauses that survive after purchase; forced redemption or forced sale; the issuer's right to freeze non-eligible holders; whether secondary venues geo-block.

failureModes.question: I am in, or become subject to, a sanctioned jurisdiction or list. Are my tokens frozen, seized, redeemable?
failureModes.lookFor: Sanctions clauses; freeze and burn powers exercised on screening hits; where seized value goes; any OFAC or FINMA-driven procedure.

failureModes.question: The venue or broker where I hold the tokens goes bankrupt. Are the tokens mine or the venue's estate?
failureModes.lookFor: Venue terms on customer asset segregation; whether the tokens sit in omnibus wallets; issuer statements about venue-held tokens; the SEC staff view on custody of tokenized securities.

failureModes.question: The venue delists the token or halts trading. Where can I sell, and can I withdraw to self-custody?
failureModes.lookFor: Withdrawal support per venue; whether the token can leave the venue at all (some are venue-internal); other venues; primary redemption as the exit.

failureModes.question: My token account is frozen by the issuer. On what grounds can that happen, with what notice, and is there an appeal?
failureModes.lookFor: Freeze grounds in the terms (KYC failure, sanctions, court order, suspicion); notice and appeal; the on-chain freeze authority and who controls it; DefaultAccountState=Frozen structures where every account starts frozen.

failureModes.question: The issuer uses the permanent delegate or a clawback to move or burn my tokens without my signature. When may it, and what do I get?
failureModes.lookFor: Permanent delegate and burn clauses; forced redemption; compensation on forced burn; any exercise recorded on-chain.

failureModes.question: The mint, freeze or delegate authority key is compromised or lost. Can tokens be minted without backing, frozen en masse, or seized? Is there a recovery path?
failureModes.lookFor: Key governance: hot key, multisig, program; key rotation history on-chain; any statement about key custody or incident response; insurance.

failureModes.question: The token program, a transfer hook or the allowlist program has a bug or is upgraded. Who controls upgrades, and is a migration to a new mint foreseen?
failureModes.lookFor: Upgrade authority of any custom program; audits; migration or token-swap clauses; incidents.

failureModes.question: Solana halts or forks. What happens to a redemption request, a corporate action or a deadline that falls in the outage?
failureModes.lookFor: Force-majeure and network-failure clauses; whether the issuer's register is on-chain or off-chain (a transfer agent's book is the record for registered shares); multi-chain issuance and bridging.

failureModes.question: The token issuer goes bankrupt. Is the underlying segregated from its estate, who enforces my claim, and roughly how long until I see anything?
failureModes.lookFor: Bankruptcy-remoteness (SPV, trust, series LLC); security interest and its agent; ring-fencing under the governing law (Swiss DLT Act, BVI, Jersey, Delaware series); the insolvency waterfall; any precedent.

failureModes.question: The issuer decides to stop (as Remora did). What notice do I get, how do I redeem, and what if I miss the window?
failureModes.lookFor: Termination and early-redemption clauses; notice periods; unclaimed-asset treatment; the Remora wind-down as the observed case.

failureModes.question: The issuer is acquired or its control changes (as Backed was by Kraken). Do my terms change, and can I redeem at that point?
failureModes.lookFor: Change-of-control clauses; the acquirer's guarantees or their absence; conflict-of-interest disclosures; whether holders get a put.

failureModes.question: A regulator acts against the issuer, the provider or a venue (licence revoked, cease-and-desist, enforcement). What happens to my holding?
failureModes.lookFor: Regulatory-change and licence-loss clauses; forced wind-down triggers; the SEC and CFTC positions on the product type; any enforcement history.

failureModes.question: The backing turns out to be short (as with the SpaceX xStocks unwind). Who bears the loss, and how is it allocated among holders?
failureModes.lookFor: Collateral ratio and top-up obligations; loss allocation; the issuer's remedies against custodians and borrowers; the observed shortfall case and how it was resolved.

failureModes.question: I ask to redeem and the issuer refuses or delays (KYC not accepted, minimum not met, gate). What are my rights?
failureModes.lookFor: Redemption conditions and the issuer's discretion; gating and suspension clauses; settlement deadlines; what a holder can do when refused.

failureModes.question: The issuer changes the terms after I bought. Can it, unilaterally? With what notice? Do I get to exit first?
failureModes.lookFor: Amendment clauses; notice mechanics; holder consent or put on amendment; the watcher's own change history for the document.

failureModes.question: The platform operator (the tokenization provider under its services agreement) fails or terminates. Can the issuer operate without it, and can I still redeem?
failureModes.lookFor: Dependence statements ('does not independently operate'); termination of the services agreement; successor provider clauses; who holds the keys.

failureModes.question: The transfer agent stops or loses its registration. Is my share still recorded, and can I convert to book-entry form?
failureModes.lookFor: Transfer-agency agreement termination; successor agent; conversion rights and timelines; whether the on-chain record or the agent's book is the register.

failureModes.question: The security agent or trustee resigns, fails or is conflicted. Who enforces the pledge for holders?
failureModes.lookFor: Agent replacement clauses; holder instruction thresholds; whether holders can enforce directly.

failureModes.question: The custodian or prime broker holding the shares goes bankrupt. Are the shares client property, insured (SIPC or equivalent), or part of the estate?
failureModes.lookFor: Custody account type (segregated, omnibus); the custodian's jurisdiction and client-asset regime; SIPC or bank-deposit protection and its limits; the issuer's disclosed custodians and any sub-custodian chain.

failureModes.question: The underlying is lent out or rehypothecated and the borrower defaults. What backs my token then?
failureModes.lookFor: Securities-lending and rehypothecation clauses; whether lent shares leave the pledge; collateral posted by the borrower; on-loan disclosure.

failureModes.question: The proof-of-reserve or attestation is wrong, stale or stops. Who is liable, and what does the issuer do?
failureModes.lookFor: Attestation scope and limitations; the attestor's liability disclaimer; what triggers a re-attestation; whether the on-chain feed can pause.

failureModes.question: The reference market is closed, halted or the oracle is stale. What price applies to trading, redemption and margin?
failureModes.lookFor: Pricing clauses for closed markets and halts; after-hours pricing; the issuer's valuation method for private companies; disputed-price procedures.

failureModes.question: The company is acquired or merged, for cash or for shares. What do I receive, and when?
failureModes.lookFor: Corporate-action clauses covering mergers; cash-out mechanics; substitution of the underlying; for synthetics, how the mark resolves.

failureModes.question: The company is delisted or goes private. Does the token terminate, and at what value?
failureModes.lookFor: Delisting and termination clauses; final valuation; timeline for cash-out.

failureModes.question: The company goes bankrupt. Do I take part in the shareholder recovery, or does the token just go to zero?
failureModes.lookFor: Whether the issuer holds and votes real shares; pass-through of proceeds; for private companies, the priority of the issuer's instrument.

failureModes.question: A split, reverse split, spin-off or rights issue happens. How is it mirrored on-chain, and what happens to the parts that cannot be (a spun-off share, a right)?
failureModes.lookFor: Multiplier and rebase mechanics; supply adjustments; treatment of non-mirrorable entitlements; observed rebases.

failureModes.question: The company pays a dividend and I do not receive it, or receive less than a shareholder would. Where does it go, and can I claim it?
failureModes.lookFor: Dividend treatment (cash, reinvested, none); timing; the multiplier increase as the payment; who keeps the difference; claims procedure.

failureModes.question: Who withholds tax on dividends, at what rate, and can I reclaim under a treaty? Who reports my holding to tax authorities?
failureModes.lookFor: Withholding rate disclosed; the entity in the chain that is the taxpayer of record; treaty access; reporting obligations (FATCA, CRS).

failureModes.question: The multiplier or supply adjustment is set wrongly (too high, too low, late). Who corrects it, and who bears the trades made in between?
failureModes.lookFor: Who controls the rebase key; correction procedures; observed multiplier changes; any disclaimer for errors.

failureModes.question: For a private company: the IPO or liquidity event happens, or never happens. What do I receive, and what if the issuer never receives proceeds?
failureModes.lookFor: Liquidity-event definitions; payout waterfall; what happens if the issuer's own holding is never converted; maturity or termination without an event.

failureModes.question: Can I vote the shares, and if not, who does? Do I receive shareholder information?
failureModes.lookFor: Voting clauses; who is the registered holder; proxy or pass-through arrangements; information rights.

failureModes.question: The law changes: the token is reclassified, banned in my jurisdiction or the issuer's exemption ends. What happens to my holding?
failureModes.lookFor: Regulatory-change clauses; forced redemption on illegality; the issuer's stated regulatory basis and what it depends on.

failureModes.question: I have a dispute. Where do I sue or arbitrate, under which law, and can I join others (class action, collective redress)?
failureModes.lookFor: Governing law and forum clauses; arbitration and class-action waivers; the entity to sue and its assets; precedent for suing an SPV in that jurisdiction.
